newsitem.title: USA: CME launches oriented strand board futures trading.
newsitem.headline: CME launches oriented strand board futures trading.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange on Friday launched its second lumber futures contract when trading began in its oriented strand board (OSB) futures.

Trading was light at the outset at 1000 CST with initial trades in the January 1997 contract at $167.00 and $168.00 per thousand square feet. The March traded at $153.00. Contract months are January, March, May, July, September and November.
Options trading will begin on Monday.
The CME has been trading futures and options on 2x4 spruce lumber since 1969.
"The wood products industry is very interested in this (OSB) contract," said Ted Bloch, president of Bloch Lumber, Chicago, during CME ceremonies preceding the launch.
OSB is a wood panel product similar to plywood and is used in roofing, flooring and sheathing of homes.

Bloch said there was as much OSB panel used in the construction of a home as lumber. He said the United States has the capacity to produce 18 billion square feet annually and it is a $3-billion-a-year industry.
The Chicago Board of Trade had a similar futures contract, but was delisted in October 1995 because of light trading volume.

"The structure of this (contract) looks a lot more positive because they are just using one product - they are going to make it a deliverable product," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst. "The Board of Trade tried to make it a hybrid plywood and two different kinds of OSB and that just didn't work."
